correctness.rationale: For y³=x⁶+a x⁴+b x²+1 in characteristic 7, distinct roots of its cubic in t=x² correspond to Δ≠0 and six simple finite branch points, giving genus four by Riemann–Hurwitz. The stated differential basis and Cartier coefficient extraction produce scalar d=2(ab+1), central c6=−Δ and determinant 3(ab+1)²Δ². Independently expanded q0(t)^2 and q0(t)^4 in GF(7)[a,b,t] and confirmed c3c9−c2c10=2(ab+1)Δ. On H=0, the 2x2 block has rank one and the semilinear stable-rank test uses B^[7]B (not BB^[7]); the vanishing scalar factors −3D(b)q(b³). Independently factored q(b³) into eight irreducible cubics with no discriminant intersection: exactly 24 distinct smooth coefficient parameters, all in degree-three Frobenius orbits, with (a-number,p-rank)=(2,1). Independently enumerated all 49² pairs in F49, finding ordinary2311/rank2 42/rank1 zero/singular48, exactly as predicted. Finite fields are not used to infer completeness over the algebraic closure.

originality.rationale: Bielliptic genus-four double-cover geometry and Frobenius/Cartier methods are established; the new assessed claim is the exact coefficient-marked GF7 7-rank stratification with degree-24 exceptional locus and Frobenius orbits. Ogasawara–Ohashi–Sakata–Harashita study superspecial double elliptic covers, which have vanishing Hasse-Witt and do not cover the smooth family’s rank-one locus via their enumerated superspecial conclusions. Borges–Gonçalves cover Fermat-type p-ranks with different parameter families. Sohn 2025 explicitly studies genus-four superelliptic a-numbers; only its abstract could be read, and authorized full-text access was blocked by disconnected VPN, so possible overlap with a-number portion is retained as a serious priority risk; it does not on present evidence resolve all stable 7-rank-one parameters.
